title: Length of lessons, beating time, and the Langley method book
summary: Clark studied with Perkins for about a year and ten months until Perkins fell sick. Perkins taught four-four and waltz time by foot, and Clark started on the Langley method.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well Mr. Russell I'll tell you. I didn't take lessons very long because he passed. I took lessons I guess about a year and ten months. And he'd taken sick. And when he'd taken sick he couldn't teach anymore. Well I was pretty well going then. Because what he put in this I kept it there. And after he passed it just looked like I didn't have confidence in anybody else to teach me. Because he used to tell me all the time the way the fellas used to make you have jitney like that. He didn't teach you that way. He taught you four full time. One, two, three, four.
Moving your foot to the side.

That's right. He taught you waltz this way. That's the way he taught you to beat waltz time. If you would forget and do this he said don't jitney here. He'd call that jitney. He didn't want you to hit your heel on the floor.
You come down on the one beat only.

You come down on the one beat. Waltz time you beat it one, two, three. One, two, three. Four full time is one, two, three, four. One, two, three, four. You always come up on the fourth beat. See? That's the way he taught you four full time.
Remember the method, the book you started in? What kind of a book it was?
Well I started in Artur Langlands. Artur Langlands.
That's right. That's what he used.
That's right. I used Artur Langlands.
